name: applySect owns the harmony, chord zero stays the tonic
summary: applySect owns the live harmony tables; chord 0 stays the tonic, chorus changes respect four-bar seams and yield to Starfall, the black hole and the finale, and no drum slot is doubled.
detail: CH[0][0] is read as "the level's tonic" by the snare body, fireDrop, the braam, the star dive, the black hole and half the sound-effect layer, at any moment in either section. The rotation CHOFF exists so a chorus can OPEN off-tonic while row slot 0 never stops being the i chord those readers assume.

name: bedTick owns the pad gain; stopping the scheduler silences nothing
summary: Stopping the scheduler does not silence continuous oscillators — bedTick is the pad's only gain owner, and replacement arrangements and pause must drive it.
detail: The bed's eight voices start once at page load and are retuned per bar, so nothing that stops scheduling NEW notes can quiet them. This has shipped wrong twice in the same shape: the drop's hush and then the black hole both arrived with the band playing straight through the thing that was supposed to have replaced it, because each added voices in the step function and touched nothing in bedTick.

name: Every pitched voice is an interval over the level's tonic
summary: Every pitched voice is an interval over its level's tonic within the natural minor vocabulary, and subF folds sub voices below 40Hz upward by octaves.
detail: The failure this exists for is a bare frequency: fireDrop's boom and braam were literal 55/110, 41.2/82.4 and 110/164.81 while the pentatonic stabs beside them transposed correctly, so half the loudest event in the game followed the key and half did not. The 40Hz fold at runtime.js:1078 exists because a phone reproduces almost nothing below it.

name: A run ends by draining its scheduler, not its rewards
summary: End-of-run cleanup drains legacy queues and special scheduler state, while real gameplay rewards are preserved separately from ephemeral audio scheduling.
detail: The two halves pull opposite ways and both have failed. Leaving a payoff, drum break or loop queue live across a death carries one run's music into the next; conflating the audio scheduling with the earned reward is how entering a black hole confiscated an armed drop whose charge had already been spent.

name: An immediate pickup needs an immediate keyed cue
summary: Immediate pickups get immediate keyed cues and overlays; a chorus that can only change at a four-bar seam is not an immediate reward signal.
detail: A section change can be most of a loop away from the moment the player took the orb, so it cannot be the acknowledgement. The hypernova star is the model: it is an overlay that adds a voice on top of whatever harmony is playing, starting on the frame it is taken, and the chorus lift it also triggers arrives later and separately.

name: The movement instrument never changes meaning
summary: The movement instrument stays consistent; authored melodies and drum fills play by themselves, with no capture or replay mode and no musical instruction banner.
detail: This is the audio side of the tap/swipe contract. A release that waits for player musical input is a release the player can fail; a banner that asks for a rhythm is an instruction that competes with the board. The authored answer phrase exists so every world's call is answered without a single input.

name: Audio is optional and never gates progression
summary: A muted game, or one where WebAudio is unavailable, must still progress and must still deliver an earned gameplay reward.
detail: The mechanism is a branch, not a wrapper: build() at runtime.js:1324-1325 arms the musical release when MU and AC exist and the context is running, and otherwise calls startStarfall() directly. Everything downstream of that branch is the same reward. A guard that returns early without the fallback is how an offline player earns something and receives nothing.

name: Content can grow past the authored frontier
summary: Levels and tiers may be added beyond the six authored levels; what is fixed is ordered thresholds, playable geometry, reachable rewards and honest lessons.
detail: A permission, not a ceiling — the frontier is a content boundary, not an exam. Breaking it ships a level whose finish line is unreachable, unlocks that fire out of order, or a banner promising an action the player cannot perform. LV currently holds six rows: dl0 0/90/215/340/470/610 with end 90/215/340/470/610/Infinity.

name: Introductions and guaranteed orbs are per run
summary: Introduction flags and guaranteed first orb placements reset per run; a level advance replays no earlier ceremony and a picked later start owes none of them.
detail: The two halves fail in opposite directions. Replaying a ceremony at every level boundary turns a climb into a loop of tutorials; carrying the flags across runs means a fresh player at a picked level 4 is shown, and charged for, introductions belonging to levels they never played. curriculum.mjs:205-219 records that the placement flags are per run and pre-spent for any guarantee whose home level sits behind a picked start.

name: MECHANICS.md and the code move together
summary: Every shipped tier and lab orb must appear in MECHANICS.md, cards change with behavior, and a lesson names only an action the player can take and a result they can see.
detail: The ledger is what the next session reads to learn what the game HAS, so a mechanic missing from it is a mechanic the next session does not know exists. Three documents in this repository once disagreed with the code at the same time, each found by a reader who trusted the prose.

name: One name per mechanic, one instruction card at a time
summary: A mechanic has one name and one live instruction card; immediate danger and a playable introduction outrank ambient announcements, and status shows only when it reads usefully.
detail: The playtest this answers counted paraphrases as separate rules: "every ring blocked", "every ring is blocked" and "gates want you to turn back" were one instruction read as three. Tier banner subs and their formation lessons are literally identical strings now. The ranking clause is the other half — a banner arriving over an incoming wall costs the player the wall.

name: Starfall is earned by three star-fed orbits and releases itself
summary: Three star-fed orbits earn Starfall (two with its upgrade); it releases automatically, runs three waves over about 9.23s, clears red and doubles collected stars. Waiting or tapping earns nothing.
detail: dropNeed() at runtime.js:1315 returns 2 with the hairtrig upgrade and 3 otherwise. build() at runtime.js:1317-1326 rejects every source that is not a completed orbit worth at least 0.04, and on the final charge arms the musical release when audio is running or calls startStarfall() directly when it is not. The 9.23s is PAYLEN = PAY * SPB/2 = 32 * (60/104)/2.

name: Tap turns, swipe changes ring, and neither is ever remapped
summary: Tap always reverses and swipe always changes ring, neither needs an aimed target, and neither may be temporarily reassigned to a melody, drum fill or echo task.
detail: This is the game's only permanent control contract, and the retired music-capture mode is what it was written against: a reward that briefly turns the turn button into an instrument leaves the player unable to steer at the exact moment the board is most crowded. The two verbs stay the two verbs through releases, drum fills, the chorus and the finale.

name: A tier is not a level
summary: Unlock ordinals come from the tier table and player-facing level names from the level table; the two ladders must never be printed as one another.
detail: The failure this exists for shipped: the death screen printed LEVEL n off the level ladder while drawing pips and deciding FURTHEST YET off the longer tier ladder, so a device whose record was level 3 could die on level 2 and be congratulated. LEVEL_MAX is defined as LV.length at runtime.js:3115 precisely so the drawn ladder cannot drift from the named one.

name: The title screen leads with art and LAUNCH, and keeps its doors reachable
summary: The title screen prioritizes Cosmo's art and its launch action; secondary doors including Learn to play and the powerup lab stay reachable on small phones.
detail: The failure is a layout one: a door that leaves the viewport or lands under another control on a 320px phone is a feature that exists only on the developer's screen. The lab bar and the pause icon have already collided once over the same corner.

name: Accounts are optional in the same sense the sound is optional
summary: Signed out, offline, blocked by an extension or served from a host with no functions behind it, the game is exactly the game and localStorage is still the real store.
detail: Nothing in the cloud path is ever between a tap and a comet moving. Every cloud promise ends in a swallowed catch; a failed request sets no error state a player has to dismiss. A native install must open its bundled title screen with no network at all — sign-in and leaderboards may report offline status but must never block a local run.

name: A leaderboard is not a reason to publish who plays
summary: Board rows carry rank, name, score, level and a timestamp; no account id and no email ever leaves the scores function.
detail: Names are bounded to twelve printable characters on the server and escaped again at the point of display, because either alone is a single point of failure for the same bug — esc() in the runtime is the only thing between a stranger's twelve characters and script execution on every other player's device.

name: Native packages bundled assets from two exact origins
summary: Capacitor packages bundled assets with no release server.url; the exact native origins are https://localhost and capacitor://localhost, and CORS stays exact.
detail: A release server.url turns the shipped app into a thin client for a URL, which breaks the offline promise and makes the store build depend on a host. The two origins are literal strings any server-side allow list must match exactly — a wildcard or a trailing-slash mismatch silently drops the native build out of every cloud feature while the web build keeps working.

name: There is one list of harnesses and it lives in the workflow
summary: A harness cannot be in tools/ without running in CI, and cannot run in CI without running under npm test; neither the runner nor any document holds its own copy of the list.
detail: Three guards close the loop: check.mjs compares tools/ against the workflow in both directions, all.mjs parses the workflow instead of listing anything, and check.mjs requires every harness filename to appear in docs/harnesses.md. Any one alone leaves the other half open.

name: A POWERUP TESTING session sends nothing but the fact that it opened
summary: The lab is suppressed inside track() rather than tagged with a property, so a lab run cannot reach the funnel and a later session's new event inherits the silence for free.
detail: Tagging would move the burden onto every future query, and the first dashboard that forgets the filter averages sandbox deaths — pinned clock, one orb on repeat, red switched off — into the real completion rate. It is also why blackhole_entered still means "a player met one in a real run", the only reading its failure rate is worth anything under.

name: Proprietary notice ships; third-party notices ship with their components
summary: Cosmo's proprietary notice and each dependency's own license must both survive into the published product; approved dependencies do not relicense the game.
detail: Two directions, both mandatory. The game is proprietary and its notice must reach the page a player loads; Phaser, TypeScript, Capacitor and the external art are under their own terms and those belong in public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt rather than absorbed into Cosmo's. That file was edited again in the living-scenery commits when world art was removed, which is exactly the kind of change nothing checks.

name: There are no passwords and no email anywhere in the system
summary: A name goes in, the server mints a uuid and 32 random bytes, and that key living in the browser is the login — a bearer token with nothing behind it and no expiry.
detail: The trade is deliberate and sized to a group of friends: the thing protected is a score on a board among people who know each other. What it costs is real and written down — signing out is a local erase, and a lost device stays signed in until the account is abandoned. Both accounts.mjs and docs/engine/cloud.md say it should be revisited before this is handed to strangers.

name: Ship the exact bundle that passed every check
summary: The Pages deploy job publishes the artifact the check job uploaded; nothing is rebuilt after the harnesses ran.
detail: A rebuild in deploy would publish bytes nothing had checked, and the build stamp would still name the same commit, so the substitution would be invisible from the outside.

name: One property name means one thing, forever
summary: A shipped telemetry property is retired rather than redefined, because redefining it silently changes what every historical row already says.
detail: run_ended once sent level holding tier+1 while level_cleared sent level holding 1-3 — one name, two scales, two events. level was retired, not redefined; tier had carried the same number all along. The same rule is why play_mode is not called mode: swipe_mode_chosen has always carried the swipe rule under that name.

name: Publish dist/ and nothing else
summary: Only dist/ is published; public/ holds intentional released material, and internal documentation, tooling and native source must never become site assets.
detail: public/ is copied verbatim into the build, so the boundary between "released" and "in the repository" is enforced at that directory rather than by intent. A stray .md, a source map or a config file in either tree is a document the world can read and a session never meant to ship.

name: Generated native source is not an APK, a binary, a device test or a signature
summary: cap sync copies assets and refreshes plugin references; the only compilation evidence in this repository is the CI debug APK, and there is none at all for iOS.
detail: The CI artifact is signed by Android's ordinary debug key, carries no owner signing secrets and is not a store upload; independent runs may use different debug keys, so an older test install may need removing first. Windows can prepare iOS project files and bundled assets and can produce no verified binary.

name: Teardown releases everything the scene acquired
summary: Scene teardown removes input and lifecycle listeners, timers, audio and graphics resources; a reload must never leave a second game running.
detail: Accumulation is the failure, and it is invisible for exactly one reload: two live scenes means doubled input and a doubled step rate, both of which read as the game suddenly getting harder rather than as a leak. Every listener the scene added — pointer, keyboard, visibility, resize, Android Back — is owned by whatever removes it.

name: The client proposes a document; the server folds it in
summary: Records are merged with per-key monotonic rules on the server, so two devices commute and a phone that has not synced since Tuesday cannot overwrite Thursday's best score.
detail: It also removes a class of tampering for free: a client that posts best:0 cannot lower anything, and the clamps stop "up" meaning 9e9. It is why the client can post without reading first, and why cloudAdopt must write with savePrefLocal rather than savePref — writing back through window.storage would be a request per frame.

name: A shared game link must be a public address
summary: Share text must name the public game URL, never location.origin, which inside a native app is a private localhost link nobody else can open.
detail: Both docs/engine/native.md and docs/engine/delivery.md state this. The code does not obey it: runSummary() ends with (location.origin+location.pathname), which on Android is https://localhost/ and on iOS capacitor://localhost/. The runtime already knows it is native and already holds CLOUD_ORIGIN, so the information to fix it is in scope. Nothing checks it.

name: A build stamp is not a deployment
summary: The build stamp identifies which source produced an artifact; a successful local build is not a live deployment, so check the published URL before reporting a release.
detail: The stamp answers "which commit is this build" and nothing else. Pages caches the plain URL for ten minutes, which is why the shipped game detects a newer stamp and swaps to it from the title screen only — reloading a live run is vandalism, and a URL already carrying the swap parameter must never redirect again or two mismatched caches bounce forever.

name: Sync the native projects last, and never call scaffolding a build
summary: Synchronize both native projects after the final web build; generating native source is not proof of an APK, an Xcode build, a device test or a signed release.
detail: The ordering matters because sync copies dist/ into the native projects, so a sync before the final build ships the previous artifact inside the app. The honesty half matters more: Android needs an SDK and JDK and iOS needs macOS, Xcode and the owner's signing credentials, none of which exist in this repository, so nothing here can produce or verify an installable build.

name: A key not in the rules table is not synced
summary: merge() iterates SYNCED_KEYS only, because an unknown key is an unbounded write into a document the server hands back to every device on the account.
detail: "Store whatever the client sends" is how a save file becomes an injection vector. Adding a synced key is a decision, not an accident. cometloop:intro and cometloop:pid are written by the game and correctly never sync.

name: Telemetry is a listener, never a dependency
summary: Every send is wrapped so a blocked host, a dead network or a thrown property can never interrupt play — and a file:// or localhost copy sends nothing at all.
detail: The silence is total by design, which is also its cost: a telemetry bug cannot be seen from inside the game and cannot reproduce in development, because TELE_OK is false on localhost and under every harness. The $pageview defect is exactly that failure mode.

name: The unsuffixed cometloop: key belongs to skill forever
summary: Historical cometloop: keys are preserved; skill records keep their unsuffixed keys and a retired mode's suffixed records may stay untouched on disk.
detail: This is what makes retiring a mode free. Every value ever written to cometloop:best and cometloop:gl was skill's, because any other mode's went to a suffixed key — so removing a mode cannot change what a stored number means on anybody's device. If recKey ever started suffixing skill, every historical record on every device would silently change owner, which is the retired cometloop:level failure exactly.

name: The lab pins the difficulty clock and hands everything back on the way out
summary: The lab pins difficulty, so any deadline based on an advancing clock needs an explicit lab policy; leaving the lab resets black-hole geometry and every timed state.
detail: A pinned clock means no tier arrives and no level ends mid-session, which is what makes the lab a calm bench rather than a run. It also means anything waiting for dl() to advance waits forever, which is why curriculum.mjs is deliberately routed away from the lab. LAB_DL is 40, which puts the shard cap on a quiet board.

name: A powerup lab session leaves the device exactly as it found it
summary: The lab may not create or alter save keys, best records, lifetime counters, lesson flags or ordinary telemetry, and a lab hop must not spend the once-ever first-hop lesson.
detail: Every guard behind this claim is a !LAB.on sitting on a line whose ordinary job is to save something, so an omitted one is invisible in a diff and looks identical to the fifteen that are there. Three of the four writes the lab originally leaked were found after the fact: hopped (which gates the first-hop rehearsal, so the lab could spend a fresh player's tutorial), groove and landed.

name: One mode ships, and MODES stays the shared tuning table
summary: Skill is the identity mode; a future difficulty is a derivative of MODES, every knob is read, and no mode silently changes curriculum, music or score rules.
detail: CHILL is retired but the table is kept at one row on purpose: the rule was arrived at rather than obvious, and a second mode that arrives while nothing is watching arrives as a branch on a flag somewhere in the game code, which is exactly what MODES exists to prevent. Every skill knob is 1, except the additive shields knob which is 0.

name: A picked start is not a climb
summary: A run started at a chosen level cannot record a climb from level 1; G.startLevel must survive a run carried legitimately between levels.
detail: This is the whole cost of letting any level be picked, and it is paid at the death screen: dying on a level you jumped to must not print FURTHEST YET, must not move the level record, and must name the picked start in the share text. The pick itself is deliberately never persisted, because a remembered selection is how a borrowed phone made friends think the game had skipped level 1.

name: The scene answers with motion and material, never a full-field flash
summary: Scene responses are bounded, ranked envelopes expressed as motion and material response; no full-field flashes or beat-driven light gain, and the default must not depend on a reduced-motion toggle.
detail: Rewritten by the living-scenery commits and now the longest bullet in the file, with its reasoning in docs/design/effects-audit.md. The black hole and major releases outrank pickups and orbits, envelopes reset across runs, and the calm ordinary state is the thing being protected: if every beat modulates the whole sky there is no headroom for the moment that matters. The new clause forbids buying calm by shipping the reduced-motion path as the default.

name: The glow is sized, normalized, edge-faded and survives context loss
summary: Glow targets stay correctly sized, blur distances in physical pixels, kernels normalized and edges faded; a lost GL context must leave visible gameplay behind.
detail: Every failure in this family is silent. A mistyped uniform name returns null from getUniformLocation and every write through it is a no-op, so one typo removes an effect with no error. A lost context makes every call a successful no-op, so the glow does not degrade, it disappears — and cannot come back unless the disc fallback is re-armed. An unguarded blur tap reads the clamped edge texel back and paints a bright rim around the whole game.

name: Each render harness answers one question, and a person still looks
summary: drawcheck owns valid canvas calls, fxcheck owns GL calls and lifecycle, rendercheck owns actual pixels; a fake context or a brightness average never establishes visual quality.
detail: The three see different things and none substitutes for another: a drawImage at the wrong translate is a valid call with finite arguments and a correct count that lands the glow three pixels off its light. The last clause is addressed to the reader rather than to CI — inspect a real frame for any visual change.

name: One composed procedural world owns the background
summary: One composed procedural world owns the background; unmarked alpha art may add material detail through the Phaser cache, but opaque plates must not replace the living scene.
detail: Rewritten in the living-scenery commits. The background is authored procedurally and stays alive; art is allowed to add material on top of it, not to become it — the world-plate webp files that used to sit in public/art/worlds were deleted for exactly that reason, and public/art/manifest.json now ships sprites only. The fallback clause is load-bearing twice: a device without WebGL gets the 2D sky, a device whose art fails to load gets the procedural layers, and both must still be the same place.

name: Reduced motion is honored without losing the message
summary: Honor the reduced-motion preference, and keep gameplay cues and labels communicating state when motion is removed.
detail: The trap is answering the preference by deleting the cue rather than restating it. A player who asked for less motion still has to know a shield was spent, a tier arrived and a reward is running, so the requirement is a second still presentation of the same state — not silence. Its sibling rule at docs/invariants.md:99-100 closes the other side: the DEFAULT must not depend on the toggle either.

name: One geometry for the backdrop, the arena and the camera
summary: radiusOf, AY and the camera transforms must match across backgrounds and gameplay; a visual accent can never change collision geometry.
detail: Two sources of truth for a radius is the detached-glow bug: an ember given a free radius so it could curve between rings left every draw pass that did not read it parked on the wrong ring — sixteen detached glows up to 89px apart on a 390px screen. The rule is inverted into a prohibition: radiusOf(ring) is the only radius an ember or an orb has, and starVisualPos is the only position a star has.

name: SKY_ARENA_CALM 0.62 and GL_MOTION 1.0, and threats stay readable
summary: The current renderer controls are SKY_ARENA_CALM = 0.62 and GL_MOTION = 1.0; hue is free but nothing may obscure a hazard in the arena.
detail: GL_MOTION was 0.25 before the living-scenery commits and is 1.0 now, described in source as seconds of visible differential sky flow rather than a beat gain; SKY_ARENA_CALM is unchanged and is how much the backdrop stands down inside the playfield band. The readability clause is the one that costs a run when it breaks: a beautiful sky that hides a red wall is a bug the player experiences as unfairness.

name: The black hole suspends powers, banks from the inner ring and pays once
summary: Ordinary timed powers suspend inside the black hole; charge grows only from settled inner-ring residence; escape opens at 12s, reaching ring 0 before 17s pays, failure forfeits it and costs a shield.
detail: The payout is once per mode, not once per arrival — no farming by hopping. Failing the deadline forfeits the bank AND spends a shield, or ends the run when there is none. BH_ESCAPE is 12 and BH_DUR is 17 in source; the prose in docs/invariants.md quotes those numbers without naming the constants, so the doc-staleness guard cannot see them.

name: The count-in runs on frames, paused time runs on the wall clock
summary: Count-in animation uses frame time and paused duration uses performance.now(); a locked phone produces no frames, and clamping a stalled frame must not erase measured wall-clock pause time.
detail: The two clocks answer different questions. A count-in is an animation and must look right at whatever frame rate exists. Paused duration is a fact about the player's day, and requestAnimationFrame does not fire at all while a tab is hidden — so an accumulator built on a clamped frame delta records the single case the field exists to detect as roughly zero.

name: Difficulty is hazard pressure per ring, not hazard count
summary: Measure hazard pressure per ring; adding a ring does not by itself prove that a mode or a level is harder.
detail: A fourth ring spreads the same shard budget over more track, so a change that raises the raw shard cap while opening a ring can be flat or even easier in the only unit the player feels. Getting this backwards is how a difficulty change ships that everyone signed off on and nobody can feel.

name: Pause freezes the world before the clock advances
summary: Pause freezes before G.t advances and is not a new gameplay state; held input is released, scheduled sound and continuous pads are silenced, and a background resume never restarts a live run silently.
detail: Pause is one early return in update(), which is what makes it cheap and also easy to get subtly wrong: the freeze either covers everything keyed off G.t or it is a live difficulty change. It must not change G.state either, or draw() renders the death screen over a live run.

name: Phaser owns the frame loop and the input, alone
summary: Phaser owns live frame scheduling and input; the runtime's standalone loop exists only for harnesses and must never run beside the Phaser loop.
detail: Two loops is not a slow game, it is a game running at double speed with doubled input, and it is invisible in every static check because both loops are individually correct. The host publishes engineUpdates, steps and frames so the ratio between them can be measured from outside.

name: Ring index 0 is the OUTERMOST orbit
summary: Ring index 0 is outermost and increasing the index moves inward; gravity and rewards must be tested against actual radius, never against an ambiguous ordinal.
detail: This exact ambiguity has shipped inverted three times in this file: a gravity pull whose comment said it dragged the comet inward walked it outward to the widest, safest, emptiest ring and parked it there; an "inner ring 2x" bonus paid on the outer ring; and the black-hole lens pushed glow away from the singularity. A reader cannot catch it, because both readings of "ring 0" sound correct.

name: The simulation is JavaScript and the docs must say so
summary: Typed host and scene contracts live in src/game/contracts.ts; src/game/runtime.js stays JavaScript and no document may claim complete type coverage.
detail: This is an honesty rule about the repository rather than a behavior of the game, and it is the kind that rots quietly: a session that moves one module to TypeScript and updates a README sentence to "fully typed" makes every later reader wrong about where type safety actually ends. The typed boundary is the contract file; everything past it is untyped by design.

name: Starfall survives a black hole and dies with the run
summary: Starfall's reward timer and waves survive a black-hole interruption without being re-earned or paid twice, and death or retry clears any abandoned Starfall state.
detail: The black hole is the one entry point that used to reach past the audio and confiscate an armed-but-unpaid release with MU.pend=null — and build() has already zeroed G.build by then, so the meter's charge went with it. Silent, and only ever to a player good enough to have earned one.

name: Telemetry property names mean one scale each, forever
summary: Telemetry uses game_level for levels, tier for unlocks and play_mode for difficulty; a historical property must never be redefined to mean another scale.
detail: Redefining a shipped property is worse than adding a wrong one, because the old rows stay in the dataset and silently change meaning: every chart spanning the change reads as a behavior shift that never happened. This is the tier-versus-level confusion again, one layer further out where nobody can see it.

name: G.t is the deadline clock, G.vt is the presentation clock
summary: G.t governs undilated run deadlines and G.vt governs presentation under slow motion; every new effect must choose its clock deliberately.
detail: Reading the wrong one is silent in both directions. A deadline on G.vt gets longer whenever the game slows down, which turns slow motion into a difficulty reduction the design never granted; an animation on G.t keeps running at full speed through slow motion and reads as a visual glitch rather than a timing bug.
